body:
## Downstream need

Downstream repos that vendor a pinned upstream dependency (realsense_ros2 pins librealsense + realsense-ros) want the bump flow to be **fully hands-off**: detect a new upstream tag -> update a single version source -> changelog -> ABI-gated auto-merge -> auto-release. Human intervention only when CI fails or the bump is potentially breaking.

Two pieces need a base decision so all downstream repos stay consistent:

### 1. Version single-source via setup.conf build-arg injection

Today the SDK version is duplicated in three places (the main Dockerfile `ARG LIBREALSENSE_VERSION`, the SDK `docker/Dockerfile.librealsense` ARG, and the pre-build hook's default), kept in sync by hand -- a bump that touches one silently drifts the others. The clean model is **one external value injected as `--build-arg` into every build**. A natural home is `setup.conf [build]`, but base's `[build]` section does not support arbitrary build-args today (only `network` etc.). Request: let `setup.conf [build]` declare build-args that `build.sh` forwards to `docker build` (main + any pre-build SDK builds).

### 2. Auto-release on an ABI-safe dependency bump

After an ABI-safe bump merges (CI green), the repo should auto-tag the next **patch** version so `release-worker` cuts a Release whose notes (sourced from `doc/changelog/CHANGELOG.md`) describe the dep bump. This needs a base convention/workflow: the versioning policy (patch on ABI-safe dep bump), the auto-tag trigger (post-merge), and the breaking-change gate (skip auto for a SONAME/minor change). Should be standardized so every downstream repo auto-releases the same way.

## Interim

realsense_ros2 implements the repo-local half now (single-source collapsed to the main Dockerfile ARG; bump script gains a CHANGELOG entry + an ABI/SONAME gate + auto-merge-when-safe) and re-aligns to whatever this issue standardizes. Downstream tracker: realsense_ros2#127.

comments.body:
**Correction to part 1 above (the "setup.conf build-arg injection" framing was wrong).**

`setup.conf` already supports arbitrary build-args -- part 1 does NOT need a new "let setup.conf declare build-args" feature. Verified in `.base`:

- `setup.conf [build]` accepts `arg_N = KEY=VALUE` entries. `setup.sh` (`_get_conf_list_sorted ... "arg_" ...`, ~L4449) turns any non-special key into a generic build-arg: it writes `KEY=VALUE` into `.env.generated` and emits `KEY: ${KEY}` into `compose.yaml`'s `build.args` (`_emit_user_build_args`). `APT_MIRROR_*` / `TZ` are just special-cased names; anything else (e.g. `LIBREALSENSE_VERSION`) is passed through.
- It even reaches the **pre-build hook**: `build.sh` `_load_env .env.generated` (~L475) runs BEFORE `_run_pre_hook` (~L553), so the hook's `${LIBREALSENSE_VERSION:-...}` picks up the setup.conf value from the env. So one `setup.conf` entry drives both the SDK pre-build and the main build -- **locally**.

**The real base gap is on the CI side, not setup.conf.** `build-worker.yaml` builds only from `inputs.build_args` (the caller's `main.yaml`); it does not run `setup.sh` or read `setup.conf` (its own comment at ~L96 notes "the local `./build.sh` flow reads from setup.conf"). So a setup.conf-driven version aligns local builds but NOT CI -> the two drift, which defeats the purpose.

**Reframed ask for part 1:** have the base **build-worker consume the downstream `setup.conf [build] arg_*` and inject them as `--build-arg`** (or otherwise let CI honor setup.conf's build-args), so a single `setup.conf` pin aligns local AND CI for every downstream repo. Downstream (realsense_ros2) will move the librealsense version pin into `setup.conf` as the single source once CI honors it; the pre-build hook is already env-first (realsense_ros2#128 / PR #129), so it needs no further change to pick up the setup.conf value.

Add to the auto-release convention: a downstream dep-bump must follow the **upstream's declared compatibility**, not bump each dependency to its own latest independently. Concrete case: realsense-ros declares its required librealsense minor in `realsense2_camera/CMakeLists.txt` (`find_package(realsense2 X.Y.0)`); the wrapper is the driver and the SDK follows it, so we never ship a version pair upstream never tested. The base convention should bless 'follow the upstream compat declaration + only auto-release upstream-sanctioned pairs' as the policy.

**Auto-release trigger mechanism (part 2) — decided: make `release-worker` directly callable with a version input; do NOT rely on a bot-pushed tag.**

The blocker for "auto-release on an ABI-safe dep bump" is GitHub's recursion guard: **events created with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not start new workflow runs** (except `workflow_dispatch` / `repository_dispatch`). So if a downstream bump workflow creates a `v*` tag using `GITHUB_TOKEN`, the tag-triggered `call-release` (`on: push: tags: 'v*'`) never fires -> no Release is cut.

Two ways out:
- **(a) PAT**: push the tag with a PAT/App token so it "looks human" and the existing `on: tags` path fires. Rejected: every downstream repo has to create + scope + rotate a secret; not org-clean.
- **(b) Direct call (chosen)**: a downstream "on bump-merge" workflow computes the next version and calls `release-worker` **directly** (`uses:`), bypassing the tag event entirely — no PAT.

**What (b) needs from base:** `release-worker.yaml` currently derives the version from the tag ref (`github.ref_name`, e.g. `prerelease: ${{ contains(github.ref_name, '-') }}`, and the Release is created for the pushed tag). Called directly from a non-tag context, `github.ref_name` is the branch, so it breaks.

Requested base change: **add an explicit `version` (or `tag`) input to `release-worker.yaml`** and use it for the release tag / name / prerelease detection, falling back to `github.ref_name` when the input is empty (keep the existing tag-triggered path working, back-compat). Then any downstream can auto-release without a PAT:

```
# downstream, on a merged bump/* PR:
jobs:
  tag:      # compute next patch vX.Y.Z+1, create+push the tag (GITHUB_TOKEN is fine for creating it)
  release:
    needs: tag
    uses: ycpss91255-docker/base/.github/workflows/release-worker.yaml@<ver>
    with:
      version: ${{ needs.tag.outputs.version }}   # <-- the new input; no tag-event dependency
```

Downstream (realsense_ros2, tracker #127) will add the bump-merge -> `uses: release-worker` workflow once base exposes the `version` input. Until then, an ABI-safe bump only auto-merges to `main` (no auto-release).

**Correction to part 1 (again): 'CI honoring setup.conf build-args' is NOT a base ask — it is the downstream repo's own job.** base already provides the controllable surface (build-worker's `build_args` input); wiring CI to read `setup.conf` and feed those inputs belongs in each downstream `main.yaml`, not in base (base should not special-case setup.conf). So part 1 has NO base component — realsense_ros2 will do the setup.conf single-source entirely repo-locally (setup.conf pin + a main.yaml step that parses it into build_args + bump targets setup.conf + Dockerfile ARG as fallback). **This issue's only base ask is part 2** (the `release-worker` `version` input for auto-release, per the comment above).

## Part 1 shipped; this issue now tracks part 2 only

Re-read against today's code. The `setup.conf` build-arg single-source
half is built and in use -- the issue's premise ("base's `[build]` section
does not support arbitrary build-args today") is no longer true.

The full path, verified end to end:

| step | where |
|---|---|
| `[build] arg_N = KEY=VALUE` is a validated schema key | `dist/script/docker/lib/schema.sh:86` (`[build.arg_]=_validate_env_kv`), prompt at `:195` |
| the `arg_N` list is split out of `[build]`, with the three known keys lifted out first | `dist/script/docker/lib/setup_cmd.sh:1130-1173` |
| each pair is written into `.env.generated` | `dist/script/docker/lib/env_emit.sh:48-49, 83` |
| each is emitted under `build.args` in `compose.yaml` | `dist/script/docker/lib/compose_emit.sh:318-321, 739-749` |

So a downstream repo can already declare one external value and have it
reach every build, which is what part 1 asked for. `realsense_ros2`'s
interim repo-local collapse can re-align onto this without waiting for
anything further from base.

**Still open, and unchanged: part 2, the ABI-gated auto-release.** That is
a genuine convention decision and needs three answers, none of which the
code above supplies:

- the versioning policy (patch on an ABI-safe dep bump)
- the auto-tag trigger (post-merge, and by what)
- the breaking-change gate (what counts as a SONAME / minor change, and
  what happens when it fires)

Note this interacts with ADR-00000027, which landed after this issue was
filed: a Z release is cut automatically and one per bug, while X and Y stay
the maintainer's and only X/Y fans out. An ABI-safe dep bump auto-releasing
a patch is consistent with that; anything that would auto-cut a Y is not.

Not renaming or rewriting the body -- the record of what was asked stays as
filed. This comment is the scope change.

title: convention: downstream dep-bump full automation (setup.conf build-arg single-source + ABI-gated auto-release)
